## OPPORTUNITIES TO SC/ST UNDER PMIS

## 38.  SHRI RAHUL GANDHI:

## SHRI P V MIDHUN REDDY:

Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state:

- (a) whether the Government has any roadmap for providing 1 crore internships over the next four years under the PM Internship Scheme (PMIS) and if so, the details thereof along with the internships planned for 2024-25;
- (b) the details of applications received, internships offered and accepted in both, round 1 and round 2 of the Scheme along with the number of youths currently doing the internship under the Scheme, State-wise and Company-wise;
- (c) whether the Government proposes to increase the stipend offered to interns and  the  details  of  funds  allocated  and  utilized  under  the  scheme  since  its inception;
- (d) whether companies are offering additional financial incentives to the interns and if so, the details thereof; and
- (e) whether Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe applicants are provided fair opportunities under the scheme and if so, the details of applications received and internships offered to SC and ST applicants?

## THE  MINISTER  OF  STATE  IN  THE  MINISTRY  OF  CORPORATE  AFFAIRS; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA):

(a): The Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) was announced in the Budget 2024-25.  It aims to provide internship opportunities to one crore youth in top 500 companies  in  five  years.  As  an  initiation  to  this  Scheme,  a  Pilot  Project  of  the Scheme targeted at providing 1.25 lakh internship opportunities in one year has

275

been launched on 03.10.2024. Guidelines containing details for Prime Minister's Internship Scheme - Pilot Project are available at https://pminternship.mca.gov.in. (b): In the round I of the Pilot Project, which commenced from 3rd October, 2024, more  than  1.27  lakh  internship  opportunities  were  provided  by  the  280  partner companies across the country. Against these, approximately 6.21 lakh applications were received from more than 1.81 lakh applicants. In this round, the partner companies made over 82,000 internship offers to over 60,000 candidates, out of which over 28,000 candidates accepted offers to join the internship. In this round, over 8700 candidates joined their internship.

In the Round  II of the PM  Internship Scheme  Pilot  Project,  which commenced on 9th January, 2025,  about 327 Partner Companies have  posted over  1.18  lakh  internship  opportunities  (new  and  edited  unfilled  opportunities  of previous  round)  across  the  country.  Against  these,  approximately  4.55  lakh applications  were  received  from  over  2.14  lakh  applicants.  As  on  15.07.2025, partner companies have made over 71000 offers. Currently, rolling out of offers and the process of acceptances/ joining by interns is in progress.

State-wise details of youth currently doing internship under the Scheme is given in the enclosed Statement- I .

Company-wise  details  of  youth  currently  doing  internship  under  the  Scheme  is given in the enclosed Statement- II .

(c): No such proposal is under consideration.

In the Budget Estimate of FY 2024-25, an amount of Rs. 2000 crores was allocated  to  Ministry  of  Corporate  Affairs,  for  the  FY  2024-25  for  PM  Internship Scheme. For the Pilot Project of the PM Internship Scheme, targeted at providing 1.25 lakh internship opportunities to the youth, an amount of Rs. 840 crore was approved.

Revised Estimate was arrived at Rs. 380 crores in the FY 2024-25. For the FY 2025-26, an amount of Rs. 10831.07 crore has been allocated.

Approximately Rs. 50 crore has been utilized under the Scheme since inception.

(d):  Under  the  Scheme,  a  one-time  grant  for  incidentals  of  Rs.6,000/-  is  to  be disbursed to the interns by the Government.  In addition, monthly assistance is to be  paid  to  the  interns,  with  Rs.  4,500/-  per  month  to  be  provided  by  the Government  and  Rs.500  per  month  by  the  Company,  from  its  CSR  funds. Expenditure associated with the training of interns under the Scheme would be borne by the company from its CSR funds, as per the extant rules.  In case any Company wishes to provide monthly assistance over and above Rs.500, it may do so  from  its  own  funds.  As  per  the  data  available  18  Companies  and  47 Companies are offering additional financial incentives under Round I &amp; Round II respectively under the PMIS Pilot Project.

(e): As per the Guidelines of the PM Internship Scheme- Pilot Project, a pool of candidates based on the number of applications, is shortlisted for each internship

276

opportunity  through  the  Portal.  The  shortlisting  process  is  aimed  at  promoting diversity  and  social  inclusivity  in  the  internship  program  through  providing  for representation of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes as well as Persons with Disabilities in the shortlist sent to the concerned company for further selection as per their respective processes and criterion.

The details of the applications received, and internships offered to SC and ST candidates in the Round I and Round II of the Pilot Project, are given in the enclosed Statement -III.

## INDIA EMPLOYMENT REPORT, 2024

## 39.     SHRI RAHUL KASWAN:

Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:

- (a) whether it is a fact that as per the India  Employment  Report  2024 (International  Labour  Organization  and  Institute  for  Human  Development), youth economic participation declined to 37 per cent in 2022 and the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) (May 2025) pegs national unemployment at 5.6 per  cent,  and  if  so,  the  details  thereof  along  with  the  updated  rural-urban unemployment rate in the country, including district-wise in Rajasthan;
- (b) whether it  is  also  a  fact  that  unemployment  in Rajasthan for the year 2020, 2022 and 2025 differs across age groups 15-24, 25-34, and 35+ years, and if so, the details thereof;
- (c) whether  the  Government  has  reviewed  the  impact  of  economic  shocks  like COVID-19 Goods and Sales Tax (GST), and demonetization on employment in rural areas of Rajasthan and if so, the details thereof;
- (d) the details of the funds allocated and utilized under the schemes like National Career Service (NCS), e-Shram and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) since 2020 along with enrollment from Churu; and
- (e) the details of the targeted employment initiatives planned for highunemployment districts in the country?

THE  MINISTER  OF  STATE  IN  THE  MINISTRY  OF  MICRO,  SMALL  AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT (KUMARI  SHOBHA KARANDLAJE):

(a) to (e): The official data source of Employment/ Unemployment indicator in India is the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) since 2017-18.

As per the latest available Annual PLFS reports, the estimated Unemployment  Rate  (UR)  on  usual  status  for  youth  of  age  15-29  years  in  the country has decreased from 17.8% in 2017-18 to 10.2% in 2023-24 which is lower than  the  global  unemployment  rate  of  youth  of  13.3  per  cent  [As  per  World Employment and Social Outlook Trends, 2024 published by International Labour Organization (ILO)].  Further, the Unemployment Rate on usual status for youth of age 15-29 years for  the State of Rajasthan has decreased from 13.4% in 202021 to 12.4% in 2023-24.

Also, MoSPI has revamped PLFS from January 2025. As per monthly PLFS reports,  the  Unemployment  Rate  (UR)  on  Current  Weekly        Status  (CWS)  for persons of age 15 years and above in rural and urban areas were 5.1% and 6.9% respectively in the month of May 2025.

As  per  the  latest  available  Annual  PLFS  reports,  the  estimated  Worker Population Ratio (WPR) on usual status for 15 years and above in the rural areas for  the  State  of  Rajasthan  has  increased  from  50.3%  in  2017-18  to  67.0%  in 2023-24 which indicates the increase in employment through various Government schemes/ programmes/ interventions.

21.07.2025

287

Under National Career Service (NCS), since Financial Year (FY)  2020-21 to FY 2025-26, a total of Rs. 375.39 crore has been allocated with an expenditure amounting to Rs. 210.88 crore (till 30th June, 2025). A total of 89,437 jobseekers were registered in the district of Churu, Rajasthan.

Under,  eShram,  as  on  15th  July,  2025,  over  30.94  crore  unorganised workers  have  already  registered  on  eShram  Portal  in  the  country  and  the  total number of registration in the district of Churu in Rajasthan is 4,27,282.

A  total  of    Rs.  1176.84  crore  were  allocated  and  Rs.  479.38  crore  were utilised under eShram scheme.

Under Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM), as on 14th July, 2025,  a  total  of  Rs.  1478.25  crore  has  been  allocated  with  an  expenditure amounting to Rs. 1308.47 crore. 458 beneficiaries are enrolled in Churu district of Rajasthan under this scheme.

Employment generation coupled with improving employability of the youth is a priority of the Government. Accordingly, Government is implementing various employment  generation  schemes/  programmes.  These  inter-alia  include  Prime Minister's  Employment  Generation  Programme  (PMEGP),  Mahatma  Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS), Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana- National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY), Rural Self Employment and Training Institutes (RSETIs), Deen Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Urban

Livelihoods  Mission  (DAY-NULM),  PM  Street  Vendor's  AtmaNirbhar  Nidhi  (PM SVANidhi),  Pradhan  Mantri  Mudra  Yojana  (PMMY),  etc.  The  details  of  various employment generation schemes/programmes being implemented by the Government may be seen at https://dge.gov.in/dge/schemes_programmes.

In  addition,  the  Union  Cabinet  has approved  the  Employment  Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme to support employment generation, enhance employability and  social  security  across  all  sectors,  with  special  focus  on  the  manufacturing sector.

## AMOUNT SANCTIONED AND UTILISED UNDER BIMA SAKHI YOJANA 40. SHRI NARESH GANPAT MHASKE:

## SHRIMATI SHAMBHAVI:

DR. SHRIKANT EKNATH SHINDE:

SHRI RAJESH VERMA:

## SHRI RAVINDRA DATTARAM WAIKAR

Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:

- (a)  the  details  of  the financial outlay,  amount sanctioned, disbursed and utilized under  the  Life  Insurance  Company's  Bima  Sakhi  Yojana  (BSY)  since  its inception;
- (b)  the  details  of  the  beneficiaries  under the  aforementioned scheme  as  of July 2025, State- wise;

- (c)  the  details  of  the  opportunities  available  for  Bima  Sakhis  to  advance  their career and the way by which the programme ensure continued support and mentorship for Bima Sakhis beyond their initial training phase;
- (d)  the  steps  taken/being  taken  to  promote  awareness  about  the  BSY  among women  in  rural  and  semi  urban  areas  for  equitable  implementation  of  the aforementioned scheme; and
- (e) whether the  Government  is considering to expand  the scope  of the aforementioned scheme to include additional roles or integrate it with other women-focused Government initiatives and if so, the details thereof ?

## THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PANKAJ CHOUDHARY):

- (a):  Bima  Sakhi-  'Mahila  Career  Agent  (MCA)  Scheme'  of  LIC  was  launched  on 9.12.2024. As such, any expense in connection with the scheme is borne by LIC. LIC  has  paid  Rs  62.36  crore  to  Bima  Sakhis  as  stipend  in  FY  2024-25.    In  the current Financial Year (2025-26), LIC has provided a budget of Rs 520 crore for the scheme, out of which Rs 115.13 crore has been paid up to 14.7.2025.
- (b):      At  present,  there  are  2,05,896  Bima  Sakhis  in  the  country.  The  State  wise data for Bima Sakhis is given in the enclosed Statement.
- (c):    LIC  provides  opportunities  to  Bima  Sakhis,  in  furtherance  of  their  career  by way  of  several  performance-based  incentives.    Graduate  Bima  Sakhis,  after

completion of  5 years, may participate in the recruitment process for the post of Apprentice Development officers of LIC, upon fulfilling the eligibility criteria.

Apart  from  above,  LIC  pays  stipend  to  Bima  Sakhis  for  first  3  years  from  their appointment  to  support  them  build  a  life  insurance  agency  career.    The  stipend scheme  is  in  addition  to  their  commission  pay-outs  and  is  subject  to  certain performance parameters.    The amount of the stipend ranges from Rs 7000/- per month in the first year to Rs 5000/- in the third year.

(d)  and  (e):  Bima  Sakhi  Yojna,  being  an  initiative  of  LIC,  is    being  promoted throughout the country from LIC's various branches and divisions, traditional and digital media and pitching in public forums.

## PROMOTION OF SPORTS AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT IN URBAN AREAS

## 42.     SHRI MANOJ TIWARI:

Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state:

- (a) the details of the schemes being implemented by the Government to promote sports and youth development in urban areas, especially in North East Delhi;

- (b) the number of sports complexes, indoor stadiums, and open gyms established/upgraded in North East Delhi under Central Government schemes since 2014;
- (c) whether any special programmes or youth engagement activities taken place under Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS) and National Service Scheme (NSS) in the North East Delhi Lok Sabha Constituency and if so, the details thereof;
- (d) whether  the  Government  proposes  to  develop  Khelo  India  Centres,  sports academies or provide coaching support to the talented youth from North East Delhi, particularly from economically weaker sections;
- (e) if so, the details thereof; and
- (f) the  total  funds  allocated  and  utilized  in  North  East  Delhi  under  various schemes of the Government during the last five years and the current year?

## THE  MINISTER  OF  LABOUR  AND  EMPLOYMENT;  AND  MINISTER  OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA):

- (a)  :  The  Government  runs  the  following major  schemes  to promote sports  and youth development in the country, including in urban areas:

The schemes under the Department of Youth Affairs are:

- (i) Rashtriya Yuva Sashaktikaran Karyakram (RYSK) is an umbrella scheme  with

the following 7 sub-schemes:

1. Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan
2. National Youth Corps
3. National Programme for Youth and Adolescent Development
4. International Cooperation
5. Youth Hostels
6. Assistance to Scouting and Guiding Organisations
7. National Young Leaders Programme
8. (ii) National Service Scheme (NSS)
9. (iii) Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Development (RGNIYD)
10. (iv) Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat)

The schemes under the Department of Sports are:

- (i) Khelo India- National Programme for Development of Sports
- (ii) Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs)
- (iii) Cash  Awards  to  Medal  Winners  in  International  Sports  Events  and  their Coaches
- (iv) National Sports Awards
- (v) Pension to Meritorious Sportspersons
- (vi) Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Sports Welfare Scheme
- (vii) National Sports Development Fund
- (viii) Running Sports Training Centres through Sports Authority of India (SAI)

The details of the above schemes are available in public domain and can be seen at https://yas.gov.in.

(b): Under the component 'Creation and Up-gradation of Sports Infrastructure' of the Khelo India Scheme, 328 sports infrastructure projects like sports complexes, stadiums etc (including 10 in the UT of Delhi at a cost of Rs. 116.23 crore) have been  sanctioned  across  the  country.  Details  of  these  projects  are  available  at https://mdsd.kheloindia.gov.in/.  Similarly,  under  National  Sports  Development Fund (NSDF), a total of 5 sports infrastructure projects, at a sanctioned cost of Rs.  9.94  Cr  have  been  supported  in  Delhi.  Further,  there  are  05  Sports  stadia located in Delhi which are being operated and administered by Sports Authority of India  (SAI)  viz.  Jawaharlal  Nehru  Stadium,  India  Gandhi  Indoor  Stadium,  Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, Dr. Shyama Prasad Mookherjee Swimming Pool Complex and Dr. Karni Singh Shooting Range.

(c): For Youth engagement activities, a total of 120 programmes, including special programmes, with a total participation of over 39,000 youth have been conducted by  NYKS  to  promote  youth  development  in  North  East  Delhi  Lok  Sabha Constituency during last FY. Further, this Ministry has been organizing 'Sundays on Cycle' programme as a regular event in Delhi with participation from diverse stakeholders  including  NSS  and  Sports  Clubs.  Around  163  events  have  been

conducted  under  'Sundays  on  Cycle'  in  Delhi  attracting  more  than  30,000 participants.

(d)  and  (e):  To  provide  coaching  support  to  the  talented  youth,  13  Khelo  India Centres  (KICs)  have  been  established  in  the  NCT  of  Delhi  wherein  07  Past Champion Athletes (PCAs) are actively supporting these Centres. NCT of Delhi also  has  01  Khelo  India State  Centre  of  Excellence  for  Athletics  and  Wrestling.

The details of these centres can be seen at https://dashboard.kheloindia.gov.in/.

(f):  Funds are allocated by this Ministry Scheme-wise, not State or District-wise. The details of the funds allocated and utilized is available on the website of the Ministry (https://yas.gov.in).

## STATUS OF PMKKS IN ANDHRA PRADESH

## 43. DR. BYREDDY SHABARI:

Will  the  Minister  of SKILL  DEVELOPMENT  AND  ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to state: -

- (a)  the  details  of  the  Pradhan  Mantri  Kaushal  Kendras  (PMKKs)  sanctioned, established and currently operational in Andhra Pradesh so far, district-wise;
- (b)  whether  it  is  true  that  most  of  the  PMKKs  set  up  in  Andhra  Pradesh  are currently nonoperational and if so, the details thereof, district-wise along with the timeline for making them functional;

- (c)  the measures taken by the Government to revive or repurpose these centres to ensure optimal utilisation of the established infrastructure;
- (d)  the details of the infrastructure, training capacity, sector-wise courses offered and enrollment numbers of operational PMKKs in Andhra Pradesh during the last five years, year wise; and
- (e)  the  total  funds  allocated,  released  and  utilised  under  PMKKs  in  Andhra Pradesh during the last five years, year and district-wise?

## THE  MINISTER  OF  STATE  OF  THE  MINISTRY  OF  SKILL  DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):

- (a):  The  district  wise  details  of  the  Pradhan  Mantri  Kaushal  Kendras  (PMKKs) sanctioned, established and currently operational in Andhra Pradesh are given in the enclosed Statement- I .

(b) and (c): Out of 23 established PMKK, 22 are operational in the State of Andhra Pradesh. The Government has undertaken several measures to ensure optimal utilisation of the established PMKK infrastructure. These include the allocation of training  targets  under  Pradhan  Mantri  Kaushal  Vikas  Yojana  (PMKVY)  and  its successor schemes. Additionally, PMKKs are encouraged to leverage Corporate Social  Responsibility  (CSR)  funding  to  support  skill  development  initiatives  and enhance the long-term sustainability of the centres.

(d):The  job  role  wise  infrastructure  and  training  capacity  of  the  PMKK  are  in accordance with the PMKK guidelines. Details of sector-wise courses offered and candidate  enrolments  in  PMKKs  across  the  State  of  Andhra  Pradesh  under PMKVY during the last five financial years (2020-21 to 2024-25) are given in the enclosed Statement- II .

(e):The district wise details of funds disbursed to PMKKs in the State of Andhra Pradesh  for  the  implementation  of  PMKVY  during  the  last  five  financial  years (2020-21-2024-25) are given in the enclosed Statement- III .

## ENVIRONMENT IMPACT OF SINKING OF HAZARDOUS CARGO IN INDIAN SEA

## 44. SHRI HIBI EDEN:

## SHRI ANTO ANTONY:

## ADV DEAN KURIAKOSE:

Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleas e to state:

- (a)   whether  the  Government  is  aware  of  the  potential  leakage  of  hazardous cargo, chemicals, or oil from sunken or damaged foreign-flagged container vessels in Indian waters, including the MSC Elsa 3 and MV Wan Hai 503, if so, the details thereof;
- (b)   whether the Government has conducted or initiated a detailed Environmental Impact  Assessment  (EIA)  following  the  sinking  of  a  container  vessel  MSC

- Elsa 3 off the coast of Kochi and the fire on a container ship MV Wan Hai 503 off the coast of Kannur, if so, the details thereof;
- (c)   whether  the  Government  has  a  Standard  Operating  Procedure  (SOP)  for dealing  with  environmental  emergencies  resulting  from  maritime  accidents such as oil spills, chemical leaks, and plastic pellet dispersal, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;
- (d)   whether  the  Government  has  invoked  the  polluter-pays  principle  to  ensure that the responsible shipping companies bear the full cost of environmental restoration, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and
- (e)   the  total  number of cases, such as oil spills, chemical leaks etc. registered under the Environmental Protection Act in the country during the last three years and the current year?

## THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH):

- (a) On 25 May 2025, MSC ELSA 3 carrying 643 containers including hazardous materials and marine fuels sank off the coast of Alappuzha. The Indian Coast Guard (ICG) is Central Coordinating Agency for Combating of Oil Pollution in the  coastal  and  marine  environment  of  various  maritime  zones.  Light  oil sheen noticed at the surface has been dispersed by the standby vessel at the site  and due  to  natural  phenomenon of wave  action. Total of 66 containers

washed  ashore  and  have  been  recovered  by  the  agency  appointed  by  the Ship  owners.  None  of  the  66  containers  were  having  hazardous  cargoes hence  there  is  no  damage  or  hazard  reported.  Around  540  MT  of  plastic nurdles  have  been  collected  from  the  Kerala  Coast  and  South  Tamil  Nadu coast.

In  the  case  of  MV  Wan  Hai  503,  the  container  vessel  suffered  fire  and explosions  approximately  44  nautical  miles  off  the  coast  of  Azhikkal  on 09.06.2025.  The  Indian  Coast  Guard,  Indian  Navy,  DG  Shipping  and  other concerned authorities have taken proactive measures to contain and mitigate any potential environmental risks.

- (b) The Ministry has requested National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management (NCSCM), Tamil Nadu to undertake a comprehensive Environment  Impact  Assessment  in  coordination  with  State  Government  of Kerala for MSC ELSA 3 incident.
- (c) The  Directorate  General  of  Shipping  has  issued  a  Standard  Operating Procedure titled 'SOP to  Handle Marine Casualty 2021', which outlines the response  framework  for  incidents  involving  shipwreck,  oil  spills,  and  other marine casualties. The Indian Coast Guard has developed a National Oil Spill Disaster Contingency Plan (NOS-DCP) for responding to Oil Spill accidents.

The NOS-DCP is a comprehensive tool, which provides a framework of co-

ordination for integrated response by various government agencies to protect the environment from deleterious effects of pollution.

- (d) In the case of MSC ELSA 3, the Kerala State Government has filed Admiralty Suit No. 12 of 2025 before the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala, seeking recovery of ₹9,531 crore from the vessel owners.
- (e) The Ministry has authorised the  State Governments viz.  the Government of the State (represented by the Secretary to the State Government incharge of environment),  Chairman  and  Member  Secretary  State  Pollution  Control Boards  (SPCBs)  and  Collector  etc.  for  the  purpose  of  the  Section  19  of Environment Protection Act (EPA), 1986 to register a case under EPA, 1986.

## e-SHRAM SCHEME IN TAMIL NADU

## 46. SHRI NAVASKANI K:

## SHRI G. SELVAM:

Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:

- (a) the details of the total number of e-Shram cards issued in the State of Tamil Nadu till date;

- (b) the details of the number of workers from various sectors registered at the portal under the e-Shram scheme in Tamil Nadu along with their breakup, gender and age-wise;
- (c) whether the Government has taken any special initiatives or awareness drives in Tamil Nadu to ensure wider registration of unorganised workers at the e-Shram portal, if so, the details thereof;
- (d) the details of welfare schemes and benefits currently being extended to eShram cardholders in Tamil Nadu including access to social security, insurance or skill development programmes;
- (e) whether the Government has identified any gaps or challenges in ensuring full coverage of eligible workers in Tamil Nadu under the e-Shram scheme; and
- (f)  if so, the details of the measures taken/being taken by the Government to address them?

THE  MINISTER  OF  STATE  IN  THE  MINISTRY  OF  MICRO,  SMALL  AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT (KUMARI  SHOBHA KARANDLAJE):

(a)  to  (f):  The  Ministry  of  Labour  and  Employment  launched  eShram  portal (eshram.gov.in)  on  26th  August  2021  for  creation  of  a  comprehensive  National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) seeded with Aadhaar. eShram portal

323

is  meant  to  register  and  support  the  unorganised  workers  by  providing  them  a Universal Account Number (UAN) on a self-declaration basis.

As on 15 th July 2025, over 30.94 crore unorganised workers have already registered  on  eShram  portal  and  over  92.87  lakhs  eShram  cards  have  been issued in the State of Tamil Nadu.

The  details  of  number  of  unorganised  workers  from  various  sectors registered on the eShram portal in Tamil Nadu along with their breakup, gender and age-wise are given in the enclosed Statement -I , II and III .

In  keeping  with  the  vision  of  the  Budget  Announcement  2024-25  on developing  eShram  as  a  One-Stop-Solution  for  unorganized  workers  to  have access to  various  social  security  schemes,  Ministry  of  Labour  and  Employment launched the eShram-'One-Stop-Solution' on 21 st October 2024. eShram- 'OneStop-Solution' entails integration of different social security/ welfare schemes at single  portal  i.e.  eShram.  This  enables  unorganised  workers  registered  on eShram to access social security schemes and see benefits availed by them so far, through eShram.

So far, fourteen (14) schemes of different Central Ministries/ Departments have already been integrated/ mapped with the eShram to extend benefits and access to social security, insurance or skill development programmes to eShram cardholders in Tamil Nadu including Pradhan Mantri Street Vendors Atmanirbhar Nidhi (PMSVANidhi), Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), Pradhan

324

Mantri  Jeevan  Jyoti  Bima  Yojana  (PMJJBY),  National  Family  Benefit  Scheme (NFBS), Mahatma  Gandhi  National  Rural  Employment  Guarantee  scheme (MGNREGS),  Pradhan  Mantri  Awas  Yojana  -  Gramin  (PMAY-G),  Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), Pradhan  Mantri  Kisan  Maan  Dhan  Yojana  (PM-KMY),  Indira  Gandhi  National Widow  Pension  Scheme  (IGNWPS),  Indira  Gandhi  National  Disability  Pension Scheme (IGNDPS), One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) and Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandna Yojana (PMMVY).

Measures  taken  by  the  Ministry  to  create  awareness  to  ensure  wider registration of unorganised workers at the eShram portal and to address gaps or challenges ensuring full coverage of eligible workers in Tamil Nadu under eShram include:

i. Holding periodic review meeting with States/UTs.

ii. Regular meeting with Common Services Centre (CSC).

iii.  To  provide  employment  and  skilling  opportunities,  eShram  is  integrated  with National Career Service (NCS) and Skill India Digital Portal.

iv.  To  facilitate  enrolment  under  pension  scheme,  eShram  is  integrated  with Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandan (PMSYM).

v. To offer one-stop search and discovery of the Government schemes, eShram is integrated with myScheme portal.

vi. SMS campaign to create awareness.

vii.  Social  media  platforms  are  also  being  used  to  spread  awareness  among workers  to  register  on  eShram.  State  Seva  Kendras  (SSKs)  and  services  of Common Service Centres are onboarded to facilitate assisted mode registrations of unorganised workers.

viii.  eShram  is  also  onboarded  on  Unified  Mobile  Application  for  New-age Governance  (UMANG  app),  to  increase  reach  among  the  workers  and  provide registration/ update facility at the convenience of their mobile.

ix. To enhance the accessibility of the eShram portal, the Ministry of Labour and Employment  launched  multilingual  functionality  on  the  eShram  portal  on  7 th January  2025,  using  the  Bhashini  platform.  This  enhancement  now  allows workers  to  interact  with  eShram  portal  in  22  Indian  languages,  improving accessibility and promoting inclusivity for all.

x.  To  make  eShram  and  associated  services,  readily  available  to  unorganized workers,  the  Ministry  of  Labour  &amp;  Employment  launched  the  eShram  mobile application on 24 th February 2025. This application provides real-time access to welfare schemes integrated with eShram, significantly improving accessibility and convenience.

## SMART CLASSROOMS UNDER SAMAGRA SHIKSHA ABHIYAN

## 47. SHRI C N ANNADURAI:

## SHRI G. SELVAM:

Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:

- (a)  the  steps  taken by  the  Government for the upgradation of computer and hitech  laboratories  and  establishment  of  smart  classrooms  in  Government schools under the Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan in the country;
- (b)  the  number  of  schools  covered  in  the  scheme  and  the  current  status  of implementation  of  these  initiatives  in  the  country  particularly  in  the  State  of Tamil Nadu;
- (c) the details of smart classrooms and upgraded hi-tech labs established in the country including Tamil Nadu during the last three years and the current year, district-wise;

- (d)  whether  any  specific  targets  have  been  set for  Tamil  Nadu  regarding  digital infrastructure in schools and if so, the details thereof, including timelines and expected learning outcomes; and
- (e)  the  steps  taken  or  proposed  to  be  taken  by  the  Government  to  ensure capacity-building of teachers, regular maintenance of digital infrastructure and technical support in schools equipped with smart classrooms and hi-tech labs in Tamil Nadu?

## THE  MINISTER  OF  STATE  OF  THE  MINISTRY  OF  SKILL  DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):

(a)  to  (e):  ICT  and  Digital  Initiatives  component  of  Samagra  Shiksha  covers Government and Government Aided Schools having classes VI to XII. Under this component financial assistance is provided for establishing ICT Labs and Smart Classrooms in schools. The non- recurring/ recurring grant under 'ICT and Digital Initiatives' is available to the States and UTs for following two options: -

Option I: Under this option schools which have not availed the ICT facility earlier can either opt for ICT or smart classrooms as per their requirement and need. In case of more than 700 enrolment, an additional ICT lab can also be considered. States/UTs have flexibility to procure hardware such as tablets/ laptops/notebooks/ integrated teaching learning devices and open source

331

operating system as well as Hardware, Software, training and resource support. This would include support for digital boards, smart classrooms, virtual classrooms and DTH channels on pro-rata basis for number of schools approved.

- i. Option  II :  Under  this  option  schools  which  have  already  availed  the  ICT facility  earlier  can  avail  smart  classrooms/tablets  as  per  the  norms  of  the scheme.

## Financial Provisions:

ICT Lab: A non-recurring grant of up to Rs. 6.40 lakh per school and recurring grant of upto Rs. 2.40 lakh per school per annum for a period of 5 years.

From  2023-24,  the  scheme  also  offers  step-wise  funding  based  on  school enrolment. (Strength &lt; 100: Rs. 2.5 Lakhs, Strength between 100 - 250: Rs. 4.5 Lakhs, Strength between 250 - 700: Rs. 6.4 Lakhs)

Smart  Classrooms: The  non-recurring  grant  for  Smart  Class  rooms  (2  smart classrooms per school) is of Rs. 2.40 lakh and the recurring grant is Rs. 38,000/per  school  per  annum  (including  E Content  and  Digital Resources,  Charges for Electricity).

The State/UT-wise details of ICT Labs and Smart Classrooms sanctioned and  functional  is  at Annexure .  As  per  UDISE+  2023-24  data,  the  district-wise details of ICT Labs and Smart Classrooms in all States/UTs including Tamil Nadu

332

from 2021-22 to 2023-24 is available on https://www.education.gov.in/en/parl_ques.

Based on the UDISE+ data and funds approved in Project Approval Board's meetings (PAB) to Stats/UTs for the year 2025-26, there were gaps identified in saturating ICT labs, smart classrooms, and subject-specific labs in Secondary and Senior Secondary Schools in States/UTs. To address this gap, a supplementary PAB was conducted on May 28, 2025 and ₹5989.90 crore was approved for the saturation of these facilities in 32 States/UTs, including Rs.34.18 crore for Tamil Nadu, for 2025-26, as per Samagra Shiksha's programmatic norms.

Education  is  in  the  Concurrent  list  of  the  Constitution  and  majority  of  the schools are under the administrative control of respective State Government and UT Administration. As per information received from State Government of Tamil Nadu,  under  Samagra  Shiksha,  13,351  ICT  Labs  and  865  Smart  Classrooms have  been  established  in  Government  Schools.  Further,  6,414  ICT  Labs  in Government  High  and  Higher  Secondary  Schools,  6,937  Hi-Tech  Labs  in Government Middle Schools and 865 Smart Classrooms in 865 Government High and  Higher  Secondary  Schools  have  been  established  and  are  functional. Capacity building training have been provided for all headmasters and teachers for technical support.

The Department of School Education and Literacy has launched a national initiative  to  improve  learning  outcomes  at  the  elementary  level  through  an

Integrated Teacher Training Programme called NISHTHA - National Initiative for School  Heads'  and  Teachers'  Holistic  Advancement  in  2019-20.  NISHTHA  is  a capacity building programme for "Improving Quality of School Education through Integrated Teacher Training". In order to provide continuous learning opportunities  to  the  teachers,  NISHTHA  online  was  launched  using  DIKSHA platform in October 2020. Teachers were oriented on various aspects related to Learning  Outcomes,  Competency  Based  Learning  and  Testing  and  ICT  in teaching-learning.

## KEEZHADI EXCAVATION FINDINGS

## 50. THIRU DAYANIDHI MARAN:

Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state:

- (a) the details of the specific scientific accuracy concerns raised by the Archaeological  Survey  of  India  that  necessitated  requesting  a  revised  report from the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology regarding the Keezhadi excavation findings;
- (b) the timeline provided to the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology for submitting the revised Keezhadi excavation report incorporating ASI's scientific accuracy requirements;

- (c)  the  details  of  the  additional  excavation  phases  and  funding  support  being provided by ASI for the tenth phase of Keezhadi excavation that began on June 18, 2024, which has already identified six terracotta pipelines and various urban settlement structures; and
- (d)  the  details  regarding  the  coordination  mechanism  established  between  ASI and  the  Tamil  Nadu  State  Department  of  Archaeology  to  ensure  scientific integrity in future excavation reports from the Vaigai river valley archaeological sites?

## THE MINISTER OF CULTURE; AND MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT):

- (a):  The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has not requested for any revised report  on Keezhadi from the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology.
- (b): Question does not arise.
- (c):  Since  2018,  Tamil  Nadu  State  Department  of  Archaeology  is  conducting excavations at the site, for which ASI does not provide any funding support.
- (d): ASI provides permission for excavations as per the provisions of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act 1958 and Rules 1959 and ensures implementation of the Act. It also provides technical support, as and when requested by any agency including State Department of Archaeology.

## RTE ACT, 2009

## 51. SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY:

Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:

- (a) whether it is a fact that the State Government of Bihar has not submitted any reimbursement claims under Section 12(1)(c) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, during the last three years;
- (b) if so, the details along with the reasons therefor;
- (c)  the details  of  States  and Union  Territories that  have claimed reimbursement under  Section  12(1)(c)  during  the  last  three  years  along  with  the  amount sanctioned and released, year-wise and State/UT-wise; and
- (d) the details of steps taken by the Government to ensure effective implementation  of  Section  12(1)(c)  of  RTE  Act  across  all  States  and  UTs, especially in States like Bihar which have not yet claimed reimbursements?

## THE  MINISTER  OF  STATE  OF  THE  MINISTRY  OF  SKILL  DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):

(a)  to  (d):    Section  12(2)  of  The  Right  of  Children  to  Free  and  Compulsory Education  (RTE)  Act,  2009  provides  for  reimbursement  to  the  Private  Unaided Schools for admitting children under Section 12(1)(c) of the said Act. In order to encourage effective implementation of aforesaid provision of the RTE Act, 2009, the  Centrally  sponsored  'Samagra  Shiksha'  provides  for  reimbursement  of  the

expenditure incurred by States/UTs. As per the programmatic and financial norms of Samagra Shiksha, the States/UTs are required to first incur expenditure from the  State  funds  towards  reimbursement  under  section  12(1)(c)  of  the  Act. Thereafter, States/UTs are to claim the funds for reimbursement from the Centre in  their  respective  Annual  Work  Plan  and  Budget  (AWP&amp;B).  Based  on  their proposal, the Project Approval Board (PAB) in the Ministry of Education approves the claim subject to, amongst other things, mandatory submission of the requisite documents in support of the claim and other programmatic &amp; financial norms of the  scheme. The State Government of Bihar has not claimed reimbursement of expenditure incurred under aforesaid provision of RTE Act, 2009 in their AWP&amp;B during the last three financial years as per PRABANDH portal.

The details of States and Union Territories that have claimed reimbursement of expenditure incurred for implementation of Section 12(1)(c) of the  RTE  Act  during  the  last  three  years  along  with  the  amount  claimed  and approved in the AWP&amp;B, year-wise and State/UT-wise are given in the enclosed

## PM-SHRI SCHOOLS IN NELLORE, AP

## 54. SHRI PRABHAKAR REDDY VEMIREDDY:

Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:

- (a)  whether the Government has selected 42 schools in Nellore district, Andhra Pradesh, as PM-SHRI schools under Phase-I;
- (b)  if  so,  the  details  of  primary,  elementary,  secondary  and  senior  secondary schools so selected out of the above 42 schools;
- (c) whether it is true that the State Govt. of Andhra Pradesh has recommended for 47 schools under the scheme;

- (d) whether it is also true that the Government has selected 80 more schools from Nellore, as PM-SHRI schools under Phase-II;
- (e) if so, the details thereof;
- (f)  whether  it  is  true  that  318  schools  from  Nellore  have  passed  after  District Verification under Phase-I of PM-SHRI scheme; and
- (g) if  so,  the steps taken/proposed to be taken by the Government to add those schools under PM-SHRI scheme?

## THE  MINISTER  OF  STATE  OF  THE  MINISTRY  OF  SKILL  DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):

(a) to (g): Under PM SHRI scheme, a total of 42 schools have been selected as PM SHRI schools through the selection process under Phase I and Phase II from the  district  of  Nellore  in  the  state  of  Andhra  Pradesh.  Of  these,  3  schools  are primary, 2 schools are elementary, 17 schools are secondary and 20 schools are senior secondary schools.

The  selection  of  PM  SHRI  schools  is  done  through  the  transparent Challenge Method. A total of 935 schools have been selected in the first, second and  seventh  phase  of  PM  SHRI  school  selection  from  the  State  of  Andhra Pradesh.

## COACHING CENTERS FOR PREPARATION OF UPSC EXAMINATION

## 57. SHRI DEEPAK ADHIKARI (DEV):

Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:

- (a)  the  number  of  coaching  centers  authorised  by  the  Central  Government  for UPSC exam in the country;
- (b) the details of coaching centers being run for preparation of  UPSC examination, State-wise; and
- (c)  the  action  taken  by  the  Government against unauthorised coaching centers, year-wise?

## THE  MINISTER  OF  STATE  IN  THE  MINISTRY  OF  EDUCATION;  AND MINISTER  OF  STATE  IN  THE  MINISTRY  OF  DEVELOPMENT  OF  NORTH EASTERN REGION (DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR):

(a) to (c): Education is in the concurrent list, the State and UT Government need to take proactive action on the matter of Coaching Institutes. In order to regulate the Private Coaching and tuition classes, a number of States/UTs have brought out  guidelines  /  regulations  /  legislations.  Majority  of  these  coaching  centers spread across the country are commercial entities which need to be regulated as per  the  law  of  the  respective  States  /  UTs.  Ministry  of  Education  has  also circulated  a  Guidelines  for  Regulation  of  Coaching  Center  to  States/UTs  on 16.01.2024.

21.07.2025

371

Department of Social  Justice  and  Empowerment,  Ministry of  Social Justice and Empowerment  runs  a  Scheme  namely  Free  coaching  for  SCs,  OBCs  and beneficiaries  of  PM  CARES  Children  Scheme,  for  imparting coaching for competitive  examinations  for  obtaining  appropriate  jobs  in  Public/Private  Sector including  Civil  Services  Examination  and/or  for  securing  admission  in  reputed technical  and  professional  higher  educational  institutions.  The  Scheme  is  being implemented  by  Dr.  Ambedkar  Foundation  through  Dr.  Ambedkar  Centre  of Excellence (DACE) established in empanelled Central Universities. As on date, a total of 19 Central Universities are empanelled under the Scheme.

The  Residential  Coaching  Academy  (RCA)  scheme  was  initiated  in  2009  by University Grants Commission (UGC) to support students from Minority communities,  SC/STs,  and  women  by  providing  them  with  equal  opportunities through  specialized  coaching.  Launched  in  select  central  universities-Aligarh Muslim  University  (AMU),  Maulana  Azad  National  Urdu  University  (MANUU), Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI), Jamia Hamdard, and Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University-the scheme  offers residential coaching for competitive exams, including  Central/State  Government  services,  banking,  and  private  sector  jobs. The scheme does not charge tuition fees but may levy nominal registration and hostel charges.

Department  of  Consumer  Affairs,  the  Central  Consumer  Protection  Authority (CCPA) imposes penalty on coaching institutes for making misleading advertisements and directs them to discontinue such advertisements.

## NATIONALLY DETERMINED CONTRIBUTIONS

## 59.   SHRIMATI MALA ROY:

Will  the  Minister  of ENVIRONMENT,  FOREST  AND  CLIMATE  CHANGE be pleased to state:

- (a)  the  details  of  the  measures taken by the Government to meet its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement; and
- (b)  the  current  status  of  the  National  Action  Plan  on  Climate Change  (NAPCC) and its eight missions?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH):

(a) and (b): The Government of India stands committed to combat climate change and  has  taken  a  number  of  measures  to  meet  India's  Nationally  Determined Contribution  (NDC)  submitted  to  the  United  Nations  Framework  Convention  on Climate Change (UNFCCC) under the Paris Agreement.

21.07.2025

375

These  measures  include  various  policies,  schemes  and  programmes  launched from time to time, to scale up India's action on both, the adaptation and mitigation fronts.  Appropriate  measures  are  being  taken  for  promotion  of  clean  energy, especially renewable energy, enhancement of energy efficiency, development of less carbon intensive and resilient urban centres, promotion of waste to wealth, safe,  smart,  and  sustainable  green  transportation  network,  creating  carbon  sink through enhanced forest and tree cover, and strengthening climate resilience in agriculture, water resources, coastal regions, health, and disaster management. India's climate action also captures citizens' contributions including those through  the  activities  under  'Mission  LiFE'  (Lifestyle  for  the  Environment) and initiatives like 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Nam.'

The  Government  is  implementing  National  Action  Plan  on  Climate  Change (NAPCC), which is the overarching framework for climate actions.  The  NAPCC comprises of nine national missions in specific areas of solar energy, enhanced energy efficiency, water, agriculture,  Himalayan Ecosystem, sustainable habitat, green  India,  human  health,  and  strategic  knowledge  on  climate  change.  The Government is also supporting States and Union Territories (UTs) for preparation of  their  respective  State  Action  Plans on Climate Change (SAPCC), in line with the  strategy  outlined  in  the  NAPCC.  To  support  the  objectives  of  NAPCC,  34 States and UTs have prepared their SAPCCs to address State specific actions. The missions under the NAPCC have been revised to align with India's Nationally

Determined Contribution (NDC) under the Paris Agreement. The missions under NAPCC are at various stages of implementation.

As a result, installed capacity of solar energy in India has increased more than 41 times, from 2.82 GW in 2014 to 116.25 GW in June 2025. India has progressively continued decoupling of economic growth from greenhouse gas emissions. The emission intensity of India's gross domestic product (GDP) has reduced by 36 per cent between 2005 and 2020.

In  June  2025,  India  has  reached  a  major  milestone  in  its  energy  transition  by achieving the NDC goal of 50% of its installed electric power capacity from nonfossil  fuel  sources;  five  years  ahead  of  the  committed  timeline  of  2030.  This remarkable  achievement  highlights  the  Government's  commitments  to  climate action and sustainable growth to become Viksit Bharat@2047. India's progress is particularly noteworthy on the global stage. Despite having one of the lowest per capita  emissions in  the  world,  India  stands  out  as  one  of  the  few  G20  nations, which are on track to fulfil or even surpass its NDC's goals.

Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:

## ASSISTANCE TO INDIAN STUDENTS ASSOCIATION ABROAD 61. SHRI KRISHNA PRASAD TENNETI:

Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:

- (a) the list of Indian Student Associations in foreign countries that are recognized by the Government of India, country-wise;
- (b)  the  details  of  financial  assistance  provided  by  the  Government  to  such Associations at abroad during the last five years and the current year, countrywise;
- (c) whether the Government has undertaken any initiative to increase collaboration with  these  Associations  for  welfare  of  Indian  students  who  are  studying  in foreign countries; and
- (d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?

## THE  MINISTER  OF  STATE  IN  THE  MINISTRY  OF  EDUCATION;  AND MINISTER  OF  STATE  IN  THE  MINISTRY  OF  DEVELOPMENT  OF  NORTH EASTERN REGION (DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR):

- (a):  Numerous  Indian  Students  Associations  exist  and  operate  in  different countries across the world. Government of India through its Embassies/Consulates abroad interacts and engages with these Indian Students Associations  for  connecting  with  the  Indian  Students  studying  in  educational institutions in their countries of accreditation. However, Government of India does not accord any formal recognition to these Indian Students Associations.
- (b):  Government  of  India,  through  its  Embassies/Consulates  abroad,  regularly support and collaborates with Indian Students Associations abroad for promoting Indian  cultural  traditions  and  students'  welfare  measures  in  foreign  countries.

21.07.2025

379

However, there is no specific financial assistance that is provided on a sustained basis to such Indian Students Associations abroad.

(c)  and  (d):  The  Indian  Students  Associations  constitute  crucial  pillars  of  the student  outreach  endeavours  and  initiatives  conducted  by  the  Government  of India.  Indian  Embassies  and  Consulates  abroad  maintain  regular  contacts  with Indian  students  and  their  Associations  enrolled  in  foreign  Universities.  This commences as soon as new Indian students are enrolled in foreign Universities. They  are  invited  to  participate  in  Welcome  Ceremonies  organized  by  Indian Embassies  and  Consulates.  Indian  Missions/Posts  also  organize  Orientation Programmes when Heads of Indian Missions/Posts brief the Indian students on challenges  and  threats,  if  any,  that  they  may  confront  during  their  stay  in  the foreign lands and how to take preventive measures. Heads of Indian Missions/Posts  and  other  senior  Embassy/Consulate  officials  also  visit  foreign Universities and Educational Institutions in their respective countries of accreditation  to  regularly  interact  with  Indian  students  and  Indian  Students Associations. During these visits and events, Indian Embassy/Consulate representatives invite Indian students to register on the relevant Government of India portals besides discussing measures to promote welfare of Indian students with  the  respective  University  authorities.  Indian  Students  Associations  abroad are increasingly playing a partner role in the efforts of this Ministry to engage with Indian students studying abroad.

## DPMUS UNDER PM VISHWAKARMA SCHEME

## 62. SHRIMATI SMITA UDAY WAGH:

Will  the  Minister  of SKILL  DEVELOPMENT  AND  ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to state:

- (a)  whether  the  Government  is  the  nodal  agency  for  implementing  the  skill component under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme and whether District Project Management Units (DPMUs) have been deployed nationwide and if so, the details of their key roles and responsibilities;
- (b)  the total number of DPMUs or District Coordinators appointed under the said scheme, State/UT and District-wise, along with their names, contact details, and office locations;
- (c)  whether any DPMU or Coordinator holds the charge of multiple districts and if so, the details thereof;
- (d)  the  process  of  payment  to  the  implementing  agencies  in  such  cases  of multiple  charge  and  whether  any  instances  of  double  payment  have  been observed and if so, the details thereof;
- (e)  whether  the  DPMUs  have  achieved  their  performance  targets  during  the current financial year and if so, the details thereof; and
- (f) the mechanism adopted by the Government for monitoring and evaluating the regular performance of DPMUs or District Coordinators?

21.07.2025

381

## THE  MINISTER  OF  STATE  OF  THE  MINISTRY  OF  SKILL  DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):

(a): Yes. As per the guidelines of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, the initiative is being jointly implemented by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME), the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), and the Department of Financial Services (DFS) under the Ministry of Finance (MoF), Government  of  India.  The  MoMSME  serves  as  the  nodal  ministry  and  is responsible  for  overall  implementation  and  coordination  of  the  Scheme.  The MSDE is tasked with overseeing the skilling component of the Scheme and has appointed  the  National  Skill  Development  Corporation  (NSDC)  as  the  Project Implementing Agency (PIA) for its execution.

District  Project  Management  Units  (DPMUs)  have  been  appointed  nationwide covering most of the districts of the country. Their key roles and responsibilities include  generating  awareness  about  the  scheme  among  the  Vishwakarma beneficiaries, informing them about the training dates, batch timings, location of training centres, benefits of the training, stakeholder coordination and facilitating their participation by guiding them to the training centres. Their role also includes regular monitoring of the training centres to ensure adherence and compliance of the training guidelines.

382

(b):  Total  number  of  DPMUs  appointed  under  the  scheme  are  497  (as  on 16.07.2025) who are covering 618 Districts of the country. DPMUs are physically present in the districts assigned to them and also make physical visits/inspection of  the  Training  Centres  to  ensure  adherence  and  compliance  of  the  training guidelines  by  the  Training  Centres.  The  State/UT  wise  details  of  497  DPMUs covering  618  Districts  is  voluminous  and  as  such  may  please  be  seen  on  the website of this Ministry at the link https://www.msde.gov.in/documents (c) and (d): Yes. 107 DPMUs have been assigned multiple districts due to specific project  requirements  and  operational  exigencies.  No  double  payment  instances have been observed as the payments are processed strictly based on the verified number of personnel deployed. The details of DPMUs who have been assigned multiple districts is voluminous and as such may please be seen on the website of this Ministry at the link https://www.msde.gov.in/documents (e): DPMUs are monitored on a task-based review system wherein daily tasks are assigned  by  the  PIA  as  per  the  program  requirements  and  the  performance  is reviewed  on  a  weekly  basis.  Moreover,  DPMUs  undergo  physical  orientation sessions  before  deployment  by  the  MSDE  and  are  further  given  training, assignment and monitoring tasks through various Physical and Virtual meetings by the PIA. They also work in close coordination with Regional Directorate of Skill

Development and Entrepreneurship (RDSDEs)  to ensure efficient  scheme

implementation at district level. Weekly tracking mechanism has also been put in place by the PIA to monitor the tasks undertaken by the DPMUs.

(f): Supervision and evaluation of DPMUs is done by the PIA on a weekly basis.

## CREATION OF GURU NANAK CIRCUIT

## 65. SHRI GURMEET SINGH MEET HAYER:

Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:

- (a)  whether the Government  is  aware  that  Guru  Nanak  Dev  Ji  travelled extensively on four Udasis  to spread  the  message of EkOnkar (One God), universal  brotherhood  and  Gurmat  (the  teachings  of  the  Guru)  as  these journeys covered vast regions in the country and beyond, leaving behind a rich spiritual and cultural legacy;
- (b)  if so, whether the Government proposed the creation of a Guru Nanak Dev Ji Circuit  under  any  scheme  to  commemorate  these  historic  journeys  and promote religious and spiritual tourism; and
- (c)  if  so,  the  details  along  with  the  steps  taken/being  taken  so  far  and  the proposed timeline for their implementation?

THE MINISTER OF CULTURE; AND MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT):

(a) to (c): Development and promotion of tourist destinations is undertaken by the respective State Government/Union Territory (UT) Administration. The Ministry of Tourism through its ongoing schemes of 'Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)', 'Swadesh Darshan' and 'Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure Development' complements the efforts of the State Governments (SGs)/UT Administrations (UTs) by extending financial assistance to SGs/UTs/Central Agencies for tourism infrastructure development. No Guru Nanak Dev Ji Circuit is under consideration of the Ministry of Tourism. However, details of projects sanctioned are given in the enclosed Statement. Receiving proposals from the State Governments/UT Administrations for financial assistance for tourism projects is a continuous process. The proposals received are examined with reference to the prescribed guidelines and financial assistance is extended for such projects subject to fulfilment of the stipulated conditions and

availability of funds.

## CONSERVATION OF THE GANGES RIVER DOLPHIN

## 66. SHRI PRADYUT BORDOLOI:

Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state:

- (a) the  details  regarding  the  current  estimated  population  of  the  Ganges  River Dolphins  in  the  Brahmaputra  and  Barak  river  basins  and  its  estimated decrease/increase during the last ten years;
- (b) the  details  regarding  the  number  of  dead  Ganges  River  Dolphins  that  have been  found  in  the  Brahmaputra  and  Barak  river  basins  during  the  last  five years along with the common causes of death that have been ascertained for them;
- (c) whether the Government has conducted any comprehensive studies on the impact of construction of dams and other infrastructure such as bridges at the

locations having more population of Ganges River Dolphins in the North-East Region and if so, the details thereof; and

- (d) the details regarding the funds allocated to the North-Eastern Region (NER) under Project Dolphin and the utilisation rates of the same, State-wise?

## THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH):

(a) : Under Project Dolphin, the first-ever comprehensive population survey of River Dolphins was conducted in the entire range of the Ganges River Dolphin in the Ganga and Brahmaputra as well as the Indus River Dolphin in the Beas river systems.  The  survey  estimated  a  population  of  6,324  (range:  5,977-6,688) Ganges  River  Dolphins.  As  per  studies  conducted  on  River  Dolphins  the population of Gangetic River Dolphin in Brahmaputra River has been reported as stable but there are no recent reports of its presence in Barak River. The details of  current  estimated populations of the Gangetic River Dolphin in Brahmaputra and Barak River basins is as given below :

|             | River Stretch                                                        | Population Estimation   |
|-------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|
| Brahmaputra | Dr. Bhupen Hazarika Setu- Hatsingimari (Indo-Bangladesh Border)      | 584 (558-610)           |
| Barak       | Sonabari (Assam-Manipur Border)- Rajartila (Indo- Bangladesh Border) | 0                       |

21.07.2025

391

(b): As reported by the state of Assam, a total of 10 cases of mortality of River Dolphins  was  found  across  various  river  systems  in  Assam  between  2020  and 2025. Various reasons like accidental killing, unknown causes, internal injury etc were ascribed to these deaths.

(c): The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has not undertaken any specific study on impact of construction of dams and other infrastructure at locations  having  more  populations  of  Ganges  River  Dolphins  in  North  East Region.  However,  the  Environment  Impact  Assessment  (EIA)  Notification,  2006 mandates a comprehensive environmental clearance process which also includes biodiversity assessments as part of the environmental impact assessment (EIA) process for dam construction projects. Further, for projects involving more than 50 ha  and  falling  within  Protected  Areas,  biodiversity  impact  assessment  report  is required for  consideration of  the  project by  the  Standing  Committee  of  National Board for Wildlife.

(d): The Ministry  of Environment, Forest and Climate Change provides financial assistance to State Governments and Union Territories under Centrally Sponsored  Scheme  'Development  of  Wildlife  Habitats'  for  conservation  and management of protected areas, conservation of wildlife outside protected areas and  recovery  programme  of  22  identified  critically  endangered  species  and  its habitats  as  per  the  Annual  Plan  of  Operations  (APO)  received  from  the  State

Governments and Union Territories and subject to availability of funds. The details of funds released for species recovery programme of Dolphin to States/UTs under the scheme during last five years are given in the enclosed Statement.

## DENOTIFICATION OF SITES UNDER AMASR ACT,1958 68.  SHRI VISHWESHWAR HEGDE KAGERI:

Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state:

- (a) the numbers of national monuments identified and listed under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeology Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act, 1958 in Uttara Kannada district, Karnataka;
- (b) whether the Government has received any request from the Member of Parliament or State Government of Karnataka for denotification of three sites viz. Kumta, Hosur, Bedkeni from the said list; and
- (c) if so, the details thereof along with the steps taken/being taken by the Government?

## THE MINISTER OF CULTURE; AND MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT):

- (a): There are 32 monuments and archaeological sites and remains declared as of national importance in district of Uttara Kannada, Karnataka.
- (b) and (c): A request has been received from Shri. Vishweshwar Hegde Kegeri , Hon'ble Member of Parliament, for de-notification of three monuments namely: (i)

The Figure of a Tiger opposite the English School at Kumta, (ii) Carved stones near  the  temple  of  the  Gram  at  Hosur,  and  (iii) Stones  (Viragals)  at  Bedkeni. Notification/Denotification  of  Monuments  from  the  list  of  Centrally  Protected Monuments is a continuous process based on the merits of the case.

## PROJECTS UNDER THE SCHEME FOR PROMOTION OF CULTURE OF SCIENCE

## 69. DR. BACHHAV SHOBHA DINESH:

Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state:

- (a) the  details  of  the  total  number  of  projects  sanctioned/proposed  by  the Government under the scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science across the country, project and State-wise, particularly in Maharashtra;
- (b) the  details  of  the  total  number  of  projects  sanctioned/proposed  by  the Government  under  the  scheme  for  Support  to  Tribal  Research  Institutes across the country, project and State-wise, particularly in Maharashtra;
- (c) the  details  of  the  total  number  of  projects  sanctioned/proposed  under  the Museum  Grant  Scheme  under  the  Umbrella  Schemes/  component  of Development  of  Museums  across  the  country,  project  and  State-wise, particularly in Maharashtra;

- (d) the  progress  of  completion  of  these  projects  along  with  the  total  funds sanctioned, disbursed and utilized, project and scheme-wise, for Maharashtra;
- (e) whether the Government has received any proposals from State Government  of  Maharashtra  or  any  Member  of  Parliament  for  same, particularly Nashik, Dhule or Malegaon during the last five years; and
- (f) if so, the details thereof along with action taken by the Government thereon?

## THE MINISTER OF CULTURE; AND MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT):

- (a): The total number of approved projects state-wise for setting up of Science Centre/City/ Innovation Hub/Digital Planetarium taken up by the National Council of  Science  Museums  (NCSM)  under  the  Scheme  for  Promotion  of  Culture  of Science  (SPoCS)  of  the  Ministry  of  Culture,  Govt.  of  India  is  listed  in  the enclosed Statement - I .

(b): Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme 'Support to Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs)' extends financial support to 29 Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) in States/Union Territories (UTs) including Tribal  Research  Institute  Maharashtra  on  the  basis  of  the  Annual  Action  Plan submitted  by  the  States/UTs  subject  to  the  approval  of  the  Apex  Committee chaired  by  the  Secretary,  Ministry  of  Tribal  Affairs.  The  details  of  the  projects sanctioned under the scheme may be seen at the official website of the Ministry

of Tribal Affairs. The link to access the same is https://tribal.nic.in/Display_Apex_Minutes.aspx.

(c):  The  details  of  total  number  of  approved  projects  state-wise  under  the Museum Grant Scheme (MGS) are given in the enclosed Statement - II. (d): The progress of completion of projects along with the total funds sanctioned, disbursed and utilized, project and scheme-wise, for Maharashtra, is given in the enclosed Statement - III.

(e) and (f): Yes. A letter dated 02 nd December, 2024 from the Hon'ble Member of Parliament  (Lok  Sabha),  Nashik,  Shri  Rajabhau  Parag  Prakash  Waje  was received regarding the establishment of a World Class Science Centre in Nashik. In its response, Hon'ble M.P. has been requested to arrange for the submission a Detailed  Project  Report  of  the  proposed  Science  Centre,  either  through  the Department of Science and Technology, Government of Maharashtra or any other Department  capable  of  operating this centre, in the prescribed format as stipulated in  the  SPoCS  guidelines,  to the Ministry of Culture for further consideration.

## FUNCTIONING ITIs IN TAMIL NADU

## 70: SHRI A. MANI:

Will  the  Minister  of SKILL  DEVELOPMENT  AND  ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to state:

- (a) the  number and details of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) functioning  in Tamil Nadu, particularly in Dharmapuri district, including the courses offered and enrolment figures;
- (b) whether the Government has assessed the quality of training and infrastructure available in ITIs, particularly in the said district and if so, the outcome of such assessments;
- (c) whether  the  Government  recognizes  the  need  to  improve  the  quality  and relevance  of  training  in  ITIs,  particularly  in  the  said  district  and  if  so,  the specific steps taken/being taken in this regard;
- (d) whether the Government proposes to establish any new ITIs at the Block or Panchayat level in Tamil Nadu, particularly in the said district and if so, the details thereof;
- (e) whether  any  specific  measures  have  been  taken  by  the  Government  to upgrade training standards, ensure industry linkage, and enhance employability of ITI graduates in Tamil Nadu, especially in the said district, and
- (f) if so, the details thereof?

THE  MINISTER  OF  STATE  OF  THE  MINISTRY  OF  SKILL  DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):

422

(a) :  The  Directorate  General  of  Training  (DGT),  under  the  Ministry  of  Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) implements the Craftsmen Training Scheme  (CTS)  through  a  country  wide  network  of  Industrial  Training  Institutes (ITIs) for the youth of the country.

At present, there are 14,615 ITIs established in the country, out of which, 3,316 are Government and 11,299 are Private ITIs.

In  the  State  of  Tamil  Nadu,  a  total  of  456  ITIs  are  currently  operational,  out  of which 93 are Government and 363 are Private ITIs. In the Dharmapuri district, 3 ITIs are functioning (Government -1 and Private - 2).

District wise enrolment of trainees in ITIs in Tamil Nadu (including Dharmapuri) in the  last  three  academic  sessions  (2022-23  to  2024-25)  in  ITIs  is  given  in  the enclosed Statement- I .

The List of courses running under CTS in ITIs in Tamil Nadu and in Dharmapuri district is given in the enclosed Statement- II .

(b) :  Establishment  and  day  to  day  administration  of  ITIs  comes  under  the jurisdiction  of  respective  State  Government  and  UT  Administration,  while  the policies  such  as  setting  the  criterion  for  affiliation,  conducting  the  examination along with certification and designing curriculum are the responsibilities of Central Government.

423

Respective State Government conducts periodic joint- inspections of  the ITIs in coordination  with  Central  Government.  Based  on  which  corrective  actions  are initiated  and  the  ITIs  that  fail  to  comply with  the  prescribed affiliation  norms  are de-affiliated.  This  ensures that only ITIs maintaining the necessary standards in infrastructure, faculty qualifications, curriculum implementation, and training delivery continue to operate.

In Dharmapuri district, some units affiliated with ITIs were de-affiliated in January 2025 due to absence of admissions over the last six academic sessions (20182023), indicating underperformance and lack of demand.

(c) : Improving the quality of training in ITIs is a continuous process. Towards this, inter-alia, the standards and norms of affiliation of ITIs are reviewed periodically. The  curriculum  of  courses  under  CTS  is  also  updated  regularly  in  consultation with industries to incorporate the latest technological advancements and industry requirements, ensuring that the skills imparted to trainees remain relevant.

Apart from these, DGT, had allocated funds under the following Schemes/Projects for upgradation of ITIs across the country including Tamil Nadu.

- i. Skill  Strengthening  for  Industrial  Value  Enhancement  (STRIVE):  Under  the STRIVE scheme, financial assistance was provided to State Governments to improve  the  relevance  and  efficiency  of  skill  development  imparted  through

Industrial Training  Institutes (ITIs)  and apprenticeship training. A  total of  500 ITIs were selected across the country, including 32 ITIs from the State of Tamil Nadu. The scheme ended on 31st May 2024, and a total financial assistance of Rs 37.82 crore was provided to the State of Tamil Nadu under this scheme. No ITI from Dharmapuri district was covered under this scheme.

- ii. Upgradation of Government ITIs into Model ITIs scheme: Under this scheme, support was extended to 35 Government ITIs across 29 States/UTs, including Tamil  Nadu.  The  scheme  ended  on  31st  March  2024,  and  a  total  financial assistance of Rs. 3.99 crore was provided to the State of Tamil Nadu for the upgradation  of  ITI  Coimbatore  under  the  Model  ITI  scheme.  No  ITI  from Dharmapuri district was covered under this scheme.

In  addition,  the  Union  Cabinet  has  also  approved  the  National  Scheme  for  ITI Upgradation and the setting up of National Centres of Excellence for Skilling to upgrade ITIs by  improving  the quality  of  training,  aligning  courses  with  industry needs, and promoting industry-led governance.

(d) :  Establishment  of  ITIs  including  start  of  new  courses  comes  under  the jurisdiction of respective State Government, whenever a proposal is received from the States/UTs for the setting up of new ITIs, it is examined and decided as per the affiliation standards and norms.

21.07.2025

425

(e) and (f)  :  Several state  governments  including Tamil  Nadu have collaborated with industries  to transform  the Government ITIs into technology centres / hubs with modern  infrastructure and  training facilities to meet  the  industry 4.0 standards. These collaborations aim to equip Government ITIs with cutting-edge technology  and  industry-aligned  curriculum  to  bridge  the  skill  gap  and  prepare students for the demands of the evolving industrial landscape.

Further,  DGT  has  also  undertaken  the  following  initiatives  to  enhance  the employability of ITI trainees across the country including in Tamil Nadu.

- i. The  curriculum of courses under CTS  is also updated  regularly in consultation with industries to incorporate the latest technological advancements and industry requirements, ensuring that the skills imparted to trainees remain relevant.
- ii. Each course under the CTS includes a compulsory subject on Employability Skills. This module focuses on essential skills such as behaviour, communication,  IT  proficiency, work  ethics, and  other attributes that enhance a trainee's ability to effectively work within a team and thrive in a professional environment.
- iii. Dual System of Training (DST) has been introduced, wherein a significant portion of the training is hands-on and conducted within the industry itself. Under  the  DST  framework,  On-the-Job  Training  (OJT)  is  provided  for  a period of 6 to 12 months within industries for courses with a total duration of

one or two years. This immersive approach integrates theoretical learning in ITIs with practical, real-world experience in industrial settings.

In the State of Tamil Nadu, DST is currently being implemented in 15 ITIs.
